name: AGM-158C LRASM
overview_md:
The AGM-158C LRASM (Long-Range Anti-Ship Missile) is the United States' modern answer to a problem it long neglected: how to sink ships at long range when the enemy can shoot back. Derived from the stealthy JASSM-ER land-attack cruise missile, it gives American aircraft and ships a precision anti-ship weapon with the range, survivability and autonomy to penetrate the layered defences of a peer navy like China's.

What sets LRASM apart is its survivability and autonomy rather than its speed. It is subsonic but low-observable, and it is designed to operate in GPS-denied, heavily jammed environments: it can navigate, identify the correct target among many, and route itself to attack using onboard sensors and threat awareness, with minimal reliance on external cueing. This addresses the reality that in a war with China, the satellite and datalink networks that normally feed targeting data may be degraded.

For an analyst, LRASM closes a genuine gap. For decades the U.S. relied on the short-ranged Harpoon while rivals fielded long-range supersonic missiles; LRASM restores a credible long-range anti-ship punch, launched from B-1B bombers, F/A-18E/F Super Hornets and (planned) F-35s and surface ships. Alongside the Maritime Strike Tomahawk and SM-6, it is a key piece of the U.S. and allied effort to hold the Chinese fleet at risk across the Western Pacific.

additional.guidance: Autonomous: INS/GPS + passive RF + imaging-IR; threat-aware routing

variants_json.name: AGM-158C LRASM
variants_json.key_changes: Stealthy autonomous anti-ship missile from JASSM-ER

combat_history.event: Achieved early operational capability on the B-1B Lancer, later the F/A-18E/F.
combat_history.significance: Restored a long-range U.S. anti-ship capability after decades of reliance on Harpoon.

modernization.description: Integration onto more platforms (incl. F-35) and capability/range increments.
modernization.impact: Multiplies the launch options and reach against ships.

vulnerabilities.description: Slower than supersonic/hypersonic rivals, giving defences more reaction time.
vulnerabilities.context: Relies on stealth and autonomy, not speed.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Long-range anti-ship strikes from bombers, fighters and ships against defended naval targets.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: B-1B raids, carrier-air-wing Super Hornets, surface combatants.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Fielded and expanding to more platforms.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The YJ-18 uses a supersonic terminal sprint; LRASM uses stealth and autonomy instead of speed.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Stealth vs speed in anti-ship missiles.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Tomahawk offers longer range from ships; LRASM offers stealthy autonomous targeting from aircraft.
NSM is a smaller, shorter-ranged stealthy anti-ship missile; LRASM is the heavy long-range option.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: The West's new anti-ship missile family.

doctrine.role: Stealthy, autonomous long-range anti-ship cruise missile to defeat peer naval defences.
doctrine.employment: Low-observable subsonic flight with autonomous target ID and routing in GPS-denied, jammed environments.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Survivability and autonomy over speed — penetrate and pick the right ship without external cueing.
doctrine.threat_context: Closes the U.S. long-range anti-ship gap and helps hold the Chinese fleet at risk in the Western Pacific.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against China's YJ-18 (speed) and alongside Maritime Strike Tomahawk and NSM.
